title: Legacy sync/generate decommission: client migration checklist & timeline
creator: Jordan Park
description: Summary: This ticket defines the requirements, acceptance criteria, and a pragmatic timeline to decommission the legacy /sync-generate and associated model aliases (legacy-model-a, legacy-stream-b). The goal is a low-friction migration path for client libraries and downstream customers while minimizing live-site risk. Background: The legacy sync/generate endpoints were retained during prior unification work to support older SDKs and partners. We are now ready to consolidate traffic onto the unified /generate endpoint and modern model aliases that support streaming, structured outputs, and function/tool calling. This document captures scope, migration steps, compatibility shims, monitoring signals, communication plan, and rollback criteria.
goals: Provide clear upgrade steps and SDK snippets for official clients (JS, Python, Go)
Ensure 99.9% successful auto-migration for first-party customers using recommended SDK versions
Remove the legacy endpoints and aliases from the hosted API with a controlled, observable rollout
Offer temporary compat shims for critical enterprise customers when needed with cutoff dates
out_of_scope: Rewriting third-party community SDKs (we will provide guidance, not maintain forks)
Model architecture changes unrelated to alias removal
requirements: Public announcement with migration timeline and documentation 8 weeks prior to cutover
Upgrade guides and code snippets for JS/Python/Go SDKs placed in Console and docs.redwood.ai
Server-side routing rule to redirect traffic from legacy endpoint to unified endpoint with header X-RW-Legacy-Redirect for telemetry during canary
Versioned SDKs released that default to unified endpoint and expose feature parity for streaming and function calls
Canary rollout with 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% phases across 2-week windows with automated health gates
Monitoring dashboards and alerting for error rates, latency, and model-quality regressions tied to evaluation prompt sets
Rollback mechanism to re-enable legacy endpoint for up to 72 hours post-cutover if critical regressions detected
acceptance_criteria: Documentation: migration guide reviewed by DevRel, Docs, and SDK owners and published
SDKs: official JS/Python/Go clients have releases with migration helpers and tests covering streaming and function calls
Routing: server-side redirect flag enabled in canary and observable via telemetry
Quality: no more than 2% delta in critical eval prompt set quality between legacy and unified endpoints during 10% canary
Stability: latency p95 increase < 20ms and error rate < 0.3% during 10% and 50% phases
Customer outreach: top 25 customers with high legacy traffic have targeted PS engagements scheduled
Final cutover: legacy endpoints disabled after 8-week notice, and a post-mortem template exists for any incidents
migration_checklist: Publish blog + Console banner announcing deprecation and timeline (8 weeks lead)
Ship SDK minor releases with migration helpers and example apps
Create Code Mod script for server-side integrations (example: replace /sync-generate -> /generate with header mapping)
Instrument telemetry to tag legacy requests and surface per-customer dashboards
Run internal canary using non-production customers and synthetic traffic
Execute staged rollout plan and verify health gates before progressing
Deactivate legacy aliases and endpoints and publish final changelog
rollout_timeline: T-56d (2026-03-10): Public announcement and docs + SDK migration snippets available
T-42d (2026-03-24): SDK releases and sample app migrations published
T-28d (2026-04-07): Start 1% canary with redirected traffic and monitoring
T-14d (2026-04-21): Evaluate canary; if healthy, progress to 10%
T-0d (2026-05-01): Final cutover to unified endpoint and disable legacy endpoints/aliases
T+7d (2026-05-08): Final sweep and archive compatibility shims; close ticket
monitoring_and_metrics: Error rate (4xx/5xx) by endpoint and model alias
Latency p50/p95/p99 for legacy vs unified endpoints
Evaluation prompt-set scoring delta and regression alerts
Number of SDK upgrades per day tracked via installer telemetry
communication_plan: 8-week public deprecation announcement (blog + Console banner + email to owners)
Weekly migration status notes in Console and updated FAQ
Targeted outreach: AE/CS to top 25 customers with >1% traffic on legacy endpoints
Post-mortem and follow-up email if rollback occurs
rollback_criteria: Sustained error rate > 1% over 30m across production traffic attributable to endpoint changes
Quality regressions > 5% on the critical eval set for two consecutive evaluation runs
Unrecoverable increase in latency (p95 increase > 150ms) affecting SLA-bound customers
implementation_notes: Engineering will expose a short-lived compatibility header X-RW-Legacy-Redirect during canary to count redirected traffic
Private customers may opt-in to extended deprecation windows; track with support tickets and PS engagements
Console will show per-customer migration progress card in the Release & Migrations section
risks: Undiscovered client forks or self-hosted SDKs that continue calling legacy endpoints
Hidden behavioral differences for edge inputs causing quality regressions
Enterprise customers behind corporate proxies that do not auto-update SDKs
